title: Quantification of polyphosphate in human cell lines using tagged PPBD peptide
author: Jiménez, Lázaro, et al.
materials: Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated goat anti mouse
Alexa Fluor 633 conjugated goat anti mouse

We used the free available software Fiji ImageJ 1.53c. As a summary, to quantify the polyP signal intensity we used the blue channel (Hoechst) to identify the nuclei and define the “regions of interest” (ROIs). These ROIs were the areas where polyP signal was quantified.6.LIF file generation:a.Go to the ImageJ toolbar: file>open>file name>open.b.The window “Bio-Formats Import options” pops up; select the following options:i.Dataset organization>open all series.ii.Color options>color mode>colorized.iii.Split into separate windows>Split channels.c.Click OK to get images from the different fluorescence channels. In this case, the blue channel is for Hoechst and green for polyP.7.ROIs selection:a.Select the Hoechst channel.b.Process>filters>Gaussian blur. Establish a value of 2 at “sigma (Radius)”. Click OK.c.Image>adjust>threshold. Select “dark background">default>over/under. Select the auto setting or manually move the sliders until all nuclei are delimitated.d.Click “apply” to obtain a binary mask.e.Process>binary>fill holes.f.Process>binary>watershed.g.Analyze>analyze particles. Click OK to get the ROIs.Note: To avoid the selection of undesired ROIs, the size of the ROI can be selected or modified to get a better automatic selection. Go to Analyze particles>size (micronˆ2). To help in a more precise selection go to Clear results>add to manager>exclude on edges.h.Opening “ROI manager” all the ROIs generated according to the selected parameters can be checked.i.Signal quantification:j.To eliminate unspecific signal apply a threshold (cut off around 50 in 8 bits images). Select the green (polyP) channel>image>adjust>threshold.k.Select “dark background”>default>over/under. Adjust the sliders manually until the unspecific signal disappear.CRITICAL: To avoid alterations in the quantification, once the threshold has been established, DO NOT click on “apply".CRITICAL: To compare the signal intensity among different quantifications (pictures, conditions, etc.).The threshold values must be the same.l.Select “ROI manager”. Click on “show all” to overlay the ROIs over the image to be quantified.m.Analyze>set measurements. Select at least “integrated density (intDent)” and “limit to threshold”. Click on “measure”.n.A new window pops up showing a table containing the results. “intDent” is the parameter used to measure the fluorescence intensity.o.For statistical significance, at least 400 cells in each of 3 independent experiments should be analyzed.We recommend the analysis of 3 independent experiments containing a minimum of 5 fields with 30–100 cells in each. For statistical significance analysis, we applied Mann-Whitney test using GraphPad Prism software.

steps.title: Produce recombinant Xpress‑PPBD peptide
steps.instruction: Generate, express, and purify 6×His‑Xpress‑PPBD peptide for polyP detection.

substeps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the E. coli Ppx1 PPBD domain (residues 306–534) using the oligonucleotides listed in the key resources table.
Clone the PPBD fragment into BamHI‑digested pRSET‑A vector (which adds a 6×His tag and Xpress tag) with the In‑Fusion HD Cloning kit; verify the construct by restriction mapping and sequencing.
Transform the plasmid into BL21 (DE3) pLysS competent E. coli cells.
Grow a single colony in 50 mL LB containing ampicillin (50 µg/mL) and chloramphenicol (25 µg/mL) for 16 h at 37 °C with agitation.
Inoculate 500 mL fresh LB with the 50 mL starter culture (same antibiotics) and incubate 2 h at 37 °C with agitation.
Add 0.5 mL of 1 M IPTG (final 1 mM) and continue incubation 6 h at 25 °C with agitation.
Centrifuge cells at 3300 rcf for 15 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant and store pellet at –80 °C (pause point).

Resuspend pellet in 40 mL cold lysis buffer (25 mM NaH₂PO₄, 150 mM NaCl, 1 % v/v Triton X‑100, 2 mM β‑mercaptoethanol, 10 mM imidazole) supplemented with lysozyme (0.4 mg/mL), 50 U benzonase, 1 mM PMSF, 1 µg/mL leupeptin, 1 µg/mL pepstatin, and 1 mM benzamidine (add lysozyme and benzonase fresh).
Incubate 15 min on ice with gentle agitation until the solution becomes less dense and nearly transparent.
Sonicate once for 30 s at 30 kHz (Dr. Hielscher, UP 50H).
Centrifuge at 3300 rcf for 10 min at 4 °C; collect supernatant.
Centrifuge the collected supernatant a second time at 3300 rcf for 10 min at 4 °C; keep the final supernatant (pellet should be very small).
Determine protein concentration by Bradford assay and dilute the supernatant to 2 mg/mL total protein.
Purify the His‑tagged peptide on a HisTrap HP 5 mL affinity column using the ÄKTA™ start system (see Materials & Equipment for buffer details).
Collect the 5 mL elution fraction with the highest imidazole concentration; inject 1 mL aliquots onto an ÄKTA HiTrap 5 mL desalting column equilibrated with 50 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 9.
Collect 1 mL fractions from desalting peaks 2 and 3 into tubes containing 100 µL glycerol; repeat for all five desalting injections (critical: work quickly to avoid precipitation).
Pool the eluate and concentrate with Amicon 10 kDa centrifugal filters to a final volume of ~1 mL (≈10‑fold concentration).
Add glycerol to reach a final concentration of 50 % v/v and store at –20 °C for several months (chosen storage condition after testing).
Optional: verify PPBD concentration and purity by SDS‑PAGE and Coomassie staining; the 6×His‑XPress‑PPBD has an apparent molecular weight of ~25 kDa.

steps.title: Prepare coverslips and seed cells
steps.instruction: Coat glass coverslips, detach, count, and seed cells to reach 60–70 % confluence after 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Place 12 mm diameter coverslips into wells of a 24‑well culture plate.
Add 90 µL of commercial poly‑L‑lysine solution to each well and incubate 1 h at room temperature (coverslip coating).
Wash each well three times with PBS.
Aspirate culture medium from the cell flask, then wash the monolayer once with 5–10 mL pre‑warmed PBS.
Add 1 mL trypsin to the flask and incubate 3 min at 37 °C in the cell incubator.
Neutralize trypsin by adding 4 mL pre‑warmed fresh culture medium, then collect the cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 3 min, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in fresh pre‑warmed medium; ensure a homogeneous single‑cell suspension (critical: avoid clumps).
Count cells and seed at a density of 8 × 10⁴ cells/mL into each poly‑L‑lysine‑coated well (≈0.8 mL per well).
Gently swirl the plate to distribute cells evenly.
Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until cultures reach 60–70 % confluence (do not exceed 70 %).

steps.title: Fix cells on coverslips
steps.instruction: Fix cultured cells with paraformaldehyde and store briefly before staining.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate culture medium from each well carefully.
Add 0.5 mL of 4 % (v/v) paraformaldehyde (p‑formaldehyde) to each well.
Incubate 15 min at 4 °C.
Wash three times with 0.5 mL PBS per wash.
Optional pause point: fixed coverslips can be kept in PBS at 4 °C for up to 1 week before proceeding.

steps.title: Immunostain polyP with PPBD
steps.instruction: Block, bind PPBD‑anti‑Xpress complex, apply secondary antibody, stain nuclei, and mount for microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Block: incubate each coverslip 1 h without shaking in 0.5 mL blocking buffer (PBS + 2.5 % v/v goat serum + 0.5 % v/v Tween‑20) at room temperature.
Prepare PPBD‑anti‑Xpress mix in blocking buffer to final concentrations of 20 µg/mL 6×His‑Xpress‑PPBD and 5 µg/mL anti‑Xpress antibody; incubate 1 h at 4 °C on a rotating shaker.
Remove blocking solution and add 250 µL of the PPBD‑anti‑Xpress mix to each coverslip; incubate 16 h at 4 °C.
Wash three times, 5 min each, with 0.5 mL PBS at 20 °C with gentle agitation.
Incubate with 0.5 mL Alexa Fluor 488 or Alexa Fluor 633 secondary antibody (diluted 1:1000 in blocking buffer) for 1 h at 20 °C with gentle agitation.
Wash three times, 5 min each, with 0.5 mL PBS at 20 °C.
Add 0.5 mL Hoechst solution (final 1 µg/mL in PBS) and incubate 5 min at 20 °C with gentle agitation.
Wash three times, 5 min each, with 0.5 mL PBS at 20 °C.
Place the coverslip face‑down onto a microscope slide with a drop of Fluoromount‑G mounting medium; protect from light.
Allow the mounting medium to dry for 1 h at 20 °C before imaging.

steps.title: Acquire confocal microscopy images
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence images of stained cells using defined Leica confocal settings.

substeps.instruction: Use a Leica DMi8 microscope equipped with a TCS SP8 confocal module and a 63× 1.4 NA HC Apo CS2 oil immersion objective.
Excite Hoechst with the 405 nm laser; excite Alexa Fluor 488 or 633 with their respective laser lines.
Set acquisition in LAS X (Leica Application Suite X) using sequential "between frames" scanning at 400 Hz.
Configure pixel size to 240.5 × 240.5 nm, image size to 246.03 × 246.03 µm, and zoom to 0.75.
Set pinhole to 1 AU for both excitation wavelengths.
Adjust laser power between 0.5 % and 2 % and PMT gain between 700 and 900; set offset between –10 and –20.
Collect emission with a PMT detector using windows: 408–475 nm (405 nm channel), 498–550 nm (488 nm channel), 648–800 nm (638 nm channel).
Fine‑tune settings to avoid photobleaching; keep laser power and gain below maximum.
Acquire at least 10 images per condition across three independent experiments.
Save images in .LIF format (compatible with LAS X and ImageJ/Fiji); optionally export as TIFF for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Quantify polyP signal using Fiji
steps.instruction: Process LIF files in Fiji/ImageJ to measure nuclear polyP fluorescence intensity.

substeps.instruction: Open the .LIF file (File > Open) and, in the Bio‑Formats Import Options dialog, select: Dataset organization → open all series; Color options → color mode → colorized; Split into separate windows → Split channels. Click OK.
Select the Hoechst (blue) channel window.
Apply Gaussian blur: Process > Filters > Gaussian Blur, sigma = 2, then OK.
Threshold the blurred image: Image > Adjust > Threshold, choose "dark background", default method, and adjust sliders until all nuclei are delineated; click "Apply" to create a binary mask.
Fill holes: Process > Binary > Fill Holes.
Separate touching nuclei: Process > Binary > Watershed.
Generate ROIs: Analyze > Analyze Particles, accept default settings, click OK; ROIs appear in the ROI Manager.
If needed, refine ROI size via Analyze > Analyze Particles > Size (µm²) and exclude edge particles (ROI Manager > Exclude on edges).
Overlay ROIs on the original image: ROI Manager > Show All.
Set measurements: Analyze > Set Measurements, check "Integrated Density" and "Limit to threshold", then OK.

Switch to the polyP (green) channel, apply a threshold to remove unspecific signal (cut‑off ≈50 on 8‑bit images) via Image > Adjust > Threshold, select "dark background", adjust manually, **do NOT click Apply** after setting the threshold.
With the same ROIs displayed, choose ROI Manager > Measure; a results table with integrated density (IntDen) for each nucleus will appear.
Repeat for all images; ensure at least 400 cells are quantified across three independent experiments (minimum 5 fields per experiment, 30–100 cells per field).
Perform statistical analysis (e.g., Mann‑Whitney test) using GraphPad Prism as described in the original protocol.
